facts.text: Applied Bayesian modeling: specify a generative model, fit the posterior with a probabilistic programming language (PPL), interrogate it with predictive checks and diagnostics, and compare alternatives. This skill is the workflow and tooling layer - it assumes Bayes' theorem and the frequentist/Bayesian contrast are already understood (see da-1-3-5, da-1-4-3).

A Bayesian model combines a prior p(θ) and a likelihood p(y|θ) into a posterior p(θ|y) ∝ p(y|θ) p(θ). For all but trivial models the posterior is intractable analytically, so we approximate it by sampling (MCMC) or optimization (variational inference). The discipline is an iterative loop - model, fit, check, expand - formalized as the Bayesian workflow (Gelman, Vehtari, Simpson et al. 2020, arXiv:2011.01808).

Use Bayesian methods when you want: full uncertainty quantification (posteriors, not just point estimates), principled regularization via priors, partial pooling across groups (hierarchical models), the ability to incorporate domain knowledge, and propagation of uncertainty into predictions/decisions.

The Bayesian workflow (iterative). Build → simulate from priors → fit → diagnose computation → check against data → compare models → expand/simplify → repeat. Treats computational failure (divergences, bad R-hat) and model misfit (failed PPCs) as distinct problems (Gelman et al. 2020; Betancourt "Principled Bayesian Workflow" 2020; Gabry et al. JRSS-A 2019).

Priors & prior predictive checks. Favor weakly-informative priors (Normal(0,1) on standardized predictors, HalfNormal/Exponential on scales, LKJ on correlations) over flat/diffuse priors. Validate via prior predictive check: draw θ from prior, simulate y, confirm plausibility (Stan Prior Choice wiki 2024; PyMC v5 docs 2024).

MCMC: HMC & NUTS. HMC uses gradients for distant, high-acceptance moves; NUTS auto-tunes trajectory length + step size and is the default in every modern PPL. Continuous params only - marginalize discrete ones (Hoffman & Gelman JMLR 2014; Betancourt arXiv:1701.02434 2017; Stan Reference Manual 2024).

Variational inference (VI/ADVI). Approximates the posterior by maximizing the ELBO - fast, scalable, but underestimates variance and can miss multimodality. ADVI automates it; normalizing flows enrich it. Validate against MCMC (Kucukelbir et al. JMLR 2017; PyMC VI docs 2024; NumPyro SVI docs 2024).

Hierarchical/multilevel models. Group-level params drawn from a shared population distribution → partial pooling (data-determined shrinkage toward the global mean). The biggest practical reason to go Bayesian (Gelman & Hill 2006; McElreath Statistical Rethinking 2020; PyMC multilevel primer 2024).

Posterior predictive checks (PPC). Simulate y_rep from the posterior predictive, compare to observed y - overlaid densities, test statistics, LOO-PIT calibration. A model that can't reproduce key data features is misspecified (Gabry et al. JRSS-A 2019; ArviZ API 2024).

Model comparison: LOO-CV (PSIS), WAIC. Compare predictive accuracy with PSIS-LOO (elpd_loo); the Pareto-k diagnostic flags unreliable points (k > 0.7 problematic). LOO preferred over WAIC for its self-diagnostics; prefer LOO over Bayes factors (Vehtari et al. Stat&Computing 2017, arXiv:1507.04544; Vehtari et al. PSIS, JMLR 2024, arXiv:1507.02646).

Convergence diagnostics. Use rank-normalized split-R-hat (target < 1.01) and bulk-ESS/tail-ESS. HMC adds divergent transitions (curvature the sampler can't resolve - reparameterize/prior fix), max-treedepth (efficiency), and E-BFMI < 0.3 (poor energy exploration) (Vehtari et al. Bayesian Analysis 2021, arXiv:1903.08008; Stan Warnings 2024).

PPLs. PyMC (Python v5+, PyTensor backend, pluggable NUTS: default/nutpie/numpyro/blackjax); Stan (reference HMC, via CmdStanPy/cmdstanr); NumPyro (JAX, fastest NUTS, GPU); Bambi/brms (formula GLMM interface y ~ x + (1|g)); ArviZ (backend-agnostic diagnostics on InferenceData) (PyMC; CmdStanPy; NumPyro; Bambi; ArviZ, all 2024).

Bayesian regression & GLMs. GLM link families carry over: Gaussian/Bernoulli/Poisson/Negative-Binomial; coefficient priors regularize (Normal≈ridge, Laplace≈LASSO, horseshoe for sparsity). Student-t likelihood for robust regression. Standardize predictors (McElreath 2020; Bambi examples 2024).
ArviZ - diagnostics & plotting hub. az.summary (R-hat/ESS/HDI), plot_trace, plot_ppc, loo/compare/plot_compare, plot_forest, plot_energy (BFMI), plot_pair (divergences) (ArviZ API 2024).
Scope & generative story. Write the model as a data-generating process; pick the likelihood family from the outcome type first.
Priors + prior predictive check. Weakly-informative priors on standardized variables; sample_prior_predictive; reject absurd priors.
Fit. NUTS, ≥4 chains. target_accept=0.8 default; raise to 0.9–0.99 on divergences. Try NumPyro/nutpie for large continuous models.
Diagnose computation. R-hat < 1.01, bulk/tail-ESS, zero divergences, E-BFMI > 0.3, no treedepth saturation. Fix here before interpreting.
Posterior predictive check. sample_posterior_predictive → az.plot_ppc, test statistics, LOO-PIT.
Compare. az.loo per model, az.compare; inspect Pareto-k.
Iterate. Expand (hierarchy/interactions/robust likelihood) or simplify; re-run.
Standardize continuous predictors (mean 0, sd 1) so default priors behave; back-transform for interpretation.

Non-centered parameterization for hierarchical models. Replace θ_g ~ Normal(μ, σ) with θ_g = μ + σ·z_g, z_g ~ Normal(0,1) (the "Matt trick") - removes the funnel that causes divergences with sparse groups (Stan User's Guide 2024; Betancourt & Girolami 2015, arXiv:1312.0906).
≥4 chains, multiple seeds, inspect trace plots - R-hat alone misses problems.
Marginalize discrete parameters so NUTS can run.
Use Bambi/brms for standard GLMMs; drop to raw PyMC/Stan only for custom structure.
Save full InferenceData (posterior + predictive + log-likelihood + sample stats) so LOO/PPCs are reproducible.
Ignoring divergences - they bias the posterior. Reparameterize, raise target_accept, or tighten priors.
Flat/diffuse "uninformative" priors as default - rarely uninformative on quantities of interest; prefer weakly-informative.
Trusting VI/ADVI without MCMC comparison - VI understates variance.
Old R-hat < 1.1 as the bar - use rank-normalized R-hat < 1.01 and check ESS.
Comparing on in-sample fit / DIC / raw likelihood - use LOO/WAIC; read Pareto-k first.
Centered hierarchical parameterization with sparse groups - the classic funnel generator; go non-centered.
Reading the posterior mean only - report HDIs, propagate the full posterior.

facts.text: A hierarchical or multilevel structure exists in the data, with per-group effects nested in an overall population, and partial pooling is preferable to treating every group independently or ignoring group structure entirely.
facts.note: AI-suggested, synthesized from this pack's existing facts — not extracted from a source document.

facts.text: Genuine prior knowledge exists, such as a previous study's effect size or a domain constraint, and should inform the estimate rather than starting from a blank slate.
facts.note: AI-suggested, synthesized from this pack's existing facts — not extracted from a source document.

facts.text: Multiple candidate models need a principled out-of-sample comparison via LOO-CV or WAIC, rather than picking whichever model fits best in-sample.
facts.note: AI-suggested, synthesized from this pack's existing facts — not extracted from a source document.

facts.text: Fit a hierarchical model with a non-centered, “Matt trick” parameterization on a small multi-group dataset and confirm it removes the divergences a centered parameterization produces.
facts.note: AI-suggested, synthesized from this pack's existing facts — not extracted from a source document.

facts.text: Run the full Bayesian workflow loop — prior predictive check, fit with NUTS across at least four chains, posterior predictive check, and model comparison via LOO-CV — on one applied dataset end to end.
facts.note: AI-suggested, synthesized from this pack's existing facts — not extracted from a source document.

facts.text: Compare a weakly-informative-prior model against a flat-prior model on the same data to see how much the prior actually shifts the posterior when data is sparse.
facts.note: AI-suggested, synthesized from this pack's existing facts — not extracted from a source document.

facts.text: Build a small model-comparison pipeline that reports Pareto-smoothed importance sampling diagnostics alongside LOO-CV, so unreliable comparisons get caught instead of trusted at face value.
facts.note: AI-suggested, synthesized from this pack's existing facts — not extracted from a source document.

facts.text: Ignoring MCMC divergences instead of treating them as a sign the posterior geometry needs reparameterization, a higher target_accept, or tighter priors — divergences bias the resulting posterior.
facts.note: AI-suggested, synthesized from this pack's existing facts — not extracted from a source document.

facts.text: Treating a flat or maximally diffuse prior as automatically uninformative, when on the actual quantity of interest after transformation it often concentrates prior mass in an unintended place.
facts.note: AI-suggested, synthesized from this pack's existing facts — not extracted from a source document.

facts.text: Trusting variational inference results without ever cross-checking against MCMC — VI is known to systematically understate posterior variance.
facts.note: AI-suggested, synthesized from this pack's existing facts — not extracted from a source document.

facts.text: Checking only R-hat and declaring convergence, instead of also inspecting trace plots across multiple chains and seeds, which catches problems R-hat alone can miss.
facts.note: AI-suggested, synthesized from this pack's existing facts — not extracted from a source document.

facts.text: MCMC sampling via HMC or NUTS is computationally expensive relative to point-estimate methods, and hierarchical models with many groups can be slow enough that VI or a data subset gets used for early iteration.
facts.note: AI-suggested, synthesized from this pack's existing facts — not extracted from a source document.

facts.text: Model comparison metrics like LOO-CV degrade when the posterior has a few highly influential observations; a bad Pareto k diagnostic signals the LOO estimate itself is unreliable, not just the model.
facts.note: AI-suggested, synthesized from this pack's existing facts — not extracted from a source document.

facts.text: The Bayesian workflow is genuinely iterative — build, fit, diagnose, check, expand — rather than a one-shot fit, which takes real analyst time compared to running a single frequentist regression.
facts.note: AI-suggested, synthesized from this pack's existing facts — not extracted from a source document.

facts.text: Weakly-informative priors are only weak relative to standardized predictors; without standardizing first, a prior tuned for one scale can be accidentally informative or accidentally uninformative on another.
